THE UNIVERSITIES ACT, No. 16 OF 1978
ORDINANCE made by the University Grants Commission under section 18 read with section 24 A of the Universities Act,No. 16 of 1978. Secretary,
University Grants Commission.
Colombo,06th December, 2017.
ORDINANCE
01. This Ordinance may be cited as the Postgraduate Institute of Indigenous Medicine Ordinance No. 05 of 2017 and shall
come into operation with effect from 06th December 2017.
02. This Ordinance shall apply to the Postgraduate Insitute of Indigenous Medicine (hereinafter referred to as the "Insitute"

established by Order made by the Minister under section 24A (1) of the Universities Act, No. 16 of 1978 (hereinafterreferred to as the "Act") and published in Gazette Extraordinary No. 2031/38 of 2017.
03. The Institute shall be attached to the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka (hereinafter referred to as the "University").
04. Subject to the provisions of the Act, and of any appropriate Instrument and the powers, duties and functions of the
University Grants Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission"), the Institute shall have power to :-

(a)admit students;

(b)provide for postgraduate instructios, training and research in specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha andUnani systems of Medicine as may be approved by the Commission upon the recommendation of theInstitute and the University.

(c)determine with the approval of the University and the concurrence of the Commission, the postgraduatedegrees, postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions to be awardedin the serveral specialities of Ayurved, Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine or relevant specialities;

(d)conduct with the approval of the University, postgraduate examinations for the purpose of ascertainingthe persons who have acquired proficiency in the several specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unanaisystems of Medicine or relevant specialities, and to recommend to the University of persons who havepassed the examinations and satisfied such other conditions as the University may prescribe by By-lawsin consultation with the Institute, are eligible for the award of postgraduate degrees, postgraduate diplomas,postgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions of the University;

(e)co-operate, by way of exchnge of teachers, students and scholars or otherwise with Universities orInstitutions in Sri Lanka or aboard, having objects similar or substantially similar to those of the Institute;

(f)recognize examinations passed and the period of learning or study pursued by persons seeking admissionto, or by students of the Institute at Universities and places of learning of university level, as beingequivalent to such examinations and periods of learning or study in the Institute, or such part thereof, asmay be prescribed by By-law, and to withdraw such recognition at any time;

(g)recommend to the University the creation, abolition or suspension of Professorships, AssociateProfessorships, Senior Lectureships, Lecturerships and other posts as may be required for the purposes ofthe Institute;
(h)erect, equip, and maintain, for the porpose of the Institute, libraries, laboratories and other buildingswhether for instructional, training or research purposes;
(i)award fellowships, scholarships, medals and other prizes in consultation with the University;
(j)make arrangements for conducting research and courses or parts of courses in places outside the Universityand the Institute in accordance with any By-law providing for the same;
(k)recognize with the concurrence of the University such persons as may be approved by the Institute, astrainers and examiners of the Institute;
(l)demand and receive fees in accordance with any Rule providing for the same; and
(m)do all such other acts and things, whether incidental to or consequent upon the powers, duties andfunctions aforesaid, in order to further the objects of the Institute;
05. The Officers of the Institute shall be the following:-
(a)the Director; and
(b)the holder of any other post declared by the Ordinance to be a post, the holder of which, is an officer forthe purpose of this paragraph.
06. (1)The first Director shall be appointed by the Commission.

(2)Every subsequent Director shall be appointed by the Commission from a panel of three persons recommended by

the Board of Management of the Institute (hereinafter referred to as the "Board"). Where a member of the staff ofa higher educational institution or a higher educational institute is appointed as Director, such institution orinstitute shall release such member of the staff so appointed to accept the post of Director:
Provided however, that no persons shall be appointed as Director of the Institute for more than two consecutiveterms.

(3)A Director shall, unless he vacates the office earlier or is removed from the office under sub paragraph (4), hold theoffice for a period of three years reckoned from the date of his appointment or until he completes his age of retirement,whichever event; occurs earlier.

(4)A Director shall be removed from the office by the Chairman of the Commission on a vote of censure pased by notles than two-thirds of the total membership of the Board, at a special meeting convened for the purpose. The memberspresent at such special meeting shall elect from among themselves a person, other than the Director, to preside atsuch special meeing.
(5)A Director who resigns or is removed from the office or completes his tenure may, if he was a member of the staff of

a higher educational institution or of a higher educational institute immediately prior to his appointment as Director,revert to his substantive post in such higher educational institution or higher educational institute,Provided that hehas not reached the age of retirement.
(6)Where the Director, by reason of leave illness, absence from Sri Lanka, or other cause is temporarily unable to

perform the duties of his office, the Commission shall, within seven days of the occurrence of such inability makesuch arrangements as it may think fit for carrying on the duties of the office of the Director. Until such arrangementsare made the Registrar of the University shall carry on the routine duties of the office.
(7)Where a vacancy occurs in the office of the Director, the Commission shall, within seven days of the occurrence of

such vacancy, make such arrangements as it may think suitable for carrying on the duties of the office of the Directoruntil a permanent appointment is made. Until such arrangements are made the Registrar of the University shall carryon the routine duties of the office.
07. (1)The Director shall be the principal executive officer and the principal academic officer of the Institue. He shall be an

ex-officio member of the Board and an ex-officio member of each Board of Study. He shall be entitled to convene, bepresent and speak at any meeting of any other Authority or body of the Institute but shall not be entitled to vote atany such meeing unless he is a member of such other Authority or body.
(2)It shall be the duty of the Director, in accordance with such directions as may from time to time be lawfully issued

to him in that behalf by the Board and each Board of Study, to ensure that the provisions of the Ordinance, the Actor any other appropriate instrument in so far as they relate to the Institute , are duly observed and effect is given tothe decisions of the Board and each Board of Study, and exercise all such prowers as he may deem necessary for thepurpose.
(3)It shall be the duty of the Director to give effect, or to ensure that effect is given to the decisions of the Board and
each Board of Study.
(4)The Director shall be the Accounting Officer of the Institute.
(5)The Director shall be responsible for the maintenance of discipline within the Institute.
08. The authorities of the Institute shall comprise of the following:-
(a)the Board;

(b)the Boards of Study;
(c)Speciality Boards; and
(d)such other bodies as may be prescribed by the Ordinance to be such authorities.
09. The Board shall be the academic and executive body of the Institute, and shall consist of the following persons:-
(1)The following ex-officio members namely:-
(a)the Director;
(b)the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister assigned the subject of Higher Education or his nominee;
(c)the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister assigned the subject of Indigenous Medecine or his nominee;
(d)the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister assigned the subject of Finance or his nominee;
(e)the Commissioner of Ayurveda;
(f)the Immediate Past Director of the Institute;
(g)the Directors of the Institute of Indigenous Medicine, Colombo established under the Act and GampahaWickramarachchi Ayurveda Institute recognised under the Act;
(h)the heads of Siddha Units, University of Jaffna and Estern University established under the Act;
(i)the Director of the Bandaranaike Memorial Ayurveda Research Institute.
(2)the following other members, namely:-
(a)One member each from among specialist grade doctors of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems ofMedicine from the Department of Ayurveda elected by the Commissioner of Ayurveda.
(b)Four members appointed by the commission from among persons who have distinguished themselves inthe fields of law, administration and finance.
(c)Two members nominated by the University Council from among the appointed members of such Council.

10. (1)The Chairman of the Board shall be the Director who shall preside at all meetings of the Board. If the Chairmanis unable to preside at a meeting the members shall select any member present to preside at such meeting.

(2)Any elected or appointed member shall, unless he vacates the office earlier, hold the office for a term of threeyears reckoned from the date of his election or appointment, as the case may be,and shall, unless removed from the office, beeligible for re - election or re - appoinment :

Provided however, that if any elected or appointed member vacates his office prior to the expiry of his term, hissuccessor shall, unless he vacates his office earlier, hold the office for the unexpired portion of the term of the office of hispredecessor:
Provided further, that each elected members shall hold the office so long as he retains the status or membershipby virtue of which he was eligible for election as a member of the Board.

(3)Any elected, member of the Board may resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to theDirector.
(4)Any appointed member of the Board may resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to theChairman of the Commission.

(5)Any elected or appointed member of the Board, who without leave of absence fails to attend three consecutivemeetings of the Board, shall be deemed to have vacated his office as a member of the Board, and the Commission shallappoint a suitable person to fill such vacancy.
(6)The members of the Board shall be paid such remuneration or allowances as the Minister shall in consultationwith the Minister assigned the subject of Finance, determine.
(7)The quorum of any meeting of the Board shall be one-third of its total membership.
(8)The Board shall meet whenever necessary, so however that it meets on not less than eight occasions in eachyear.

(9)The Director shall whenever he thinks necessary or within one week upon the receipt by him of a written requestfrom not less than one - third of the total membership of the Board,convence a special meeting of the Board.

11. (1)Subjects to the provisions of the Act and of any appropriate instrument, the Board shall exercise the powers andperform and discharge the duties and functions conferred or imposed on,or assigned to, the Institute by this Ordinance.
(2)Subject to the provisions of the Act and of any appropriate instrument, the Board shall have control and generaldirection of instructon, education, research and examinations in the Institute.
(3)Without prejudice to the generality of the powers conferred upon it by sub-paragraphs (1) and (2) the Boardshall exercise, perform and discharge the following powers, duties and functions :-
(a)to hold, control and administer the property and funds of the Institute ;
(b)to regulate and determine all matters concerning the Institute in accordance with the provisions of theAct and of any appropriate instrument ;
(c)to administer any funds made available to the Institute for its general administration and managementand any other specific purposes;
(d)to receive and accept with the concurrence of the Commission, bequests, donations and grants ofproperty both movable or immovable made to the Institute ;
(e)to evaluate the annual report and the audited accounts of the Institute and to submit such report andsuch accounts to the University and the Commission;
(f)to prepare the financial estimates of the Institute and to submit such estimates to the University and theCommission;

(g)to recommend to the University, in consultation with the relevant Board of Study, the postgraduatedegrees, postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions which shallbe awarded in the specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine, and the courses ofstudy and training to be followed, the examinations to be passed and the other conditions to be satisfiedby students who wish to qualify for such postgraduate degrees, postgraduate diplomas, postgraduatecertificates and other academic distinctions ;

(h)to recommend to the University, in consultation with the Board of Study concerned, the procedure inobtaining Board certifications in respect of a candidate's specialisation;
(i)to draft By - laws or rules for any matter in respect of which By-laws or rules are authorised to be madeand to submit such drafts to the Senate and the Council of the University for enactment:
Provided however, that no By-laws relating to courses of study and examinations shall be draftedexcept after consideration of reports from the Board of Study concerned;
(j)to provide buildings, premises, furniture, equipment and other materials needed for carrying on the workof the Institute;
(k)to recommend to the Senate of the University in consultation with the relevant Board of Study, suchpersons as are suitable for recognition as trainers and examiners of the Institute;
(l)to recommend to the Commission, after consideration of reports from the relevant Board of Study andwith the approval of the University -
(i)schemes for the re-organization of existing Boards of Study and Speciality Boards, and the estab-lishment of new Boards of Study and Speciality Boards; and
(ii)the assignments of specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine to the respec-tive Boards of Study ;

(m)to appoint such number of Standing Committees or ad hoc Committees as it may deem fit, and to specifytheir terms of reference; to consider the reports of such committees and to either approve such reportswhether with or without modification, or to reject such reports;
(n)to determine, in consultation with the relevant Board of Study and with the concurrence of the Univer-sity, the requirements for the admission of students to courses of study;

(o)to invest any moneys belonging to the Institute including any unapplied income, in any Security interms of the provisions of section 20 of the Trust Ordinance or any other written law, and to invest suchmoneys,with the approval of the Commission in the purchase of immovable property in Sri Lanka or varysuch investments or to place in fixed deposits in any bank approved by the Commission, any portion ofsuch moneys not required for immediate expenditure; and
(p)to exercise all other powers of the Institute, which are incidental to or consequential upon the powers ofthe Institute as provided for in this Ordinance or any other appropriate instrument.

(4)No resolution shall be passed by the Board in relation to any academic matter unless the appropriate Board ofStudy has first been given an opportunity of recording and conveying its opinion thereon to the Board:
Provided that, no resolution so passed shall be acted upon except with the concurrence of the University.
In this paragragh, ''academic matter'' means any matter which is subject to the control and general direction of theappropriate Board of Study.
(12)The Board shall establish Boards of Study for each of the following systems of Medicine and Specialty Boardsunder the relevant Boards of Study : -
(a)Ayurveda Medicine;
(b)Siddha Medicine; and
(c)Unani Medicine.

13. (1)The Board of Study of Ayurveda Medicine shall consist of the following persons :-
(a)the Director who shall be an ex-officio member;

(b)two members from the branch of Ayurveda of the Institute of Indigenous Medicine, Colombo establishedunder the Act, elected from among the Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors, and SeniorLecturers at the meeting chaired by the Director of the Institute;

(c)two members from the Gampaha Wickramarachchi Ayurveda Institute recognised under the Act, electedfrom among the Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors, and Senior Lecturers at the meetingchaired by the Director of the Institute;

(d)Senior Professor, Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Lecturer from each Departments of study of :-(i)Kaya Chikitsa;(ii)Shalya Shalakya;(iii)Prasutitantra Kaumarabhrithya;(iv)Deshiya Chikitsa;(v)Swastha Vrittha;(vi)Dravya Guna Vignana;(vii)Shareera Vignana;(viii)Maulika Siddhanta,

In the Institute of Indigenous Medicine, Colombo established under the Act and Gampaha WickramarachchiAyurveda Institute recognised under the Act, nominated by the Director of the relevant Institute in that order on therecommendation of the relevant Department of Study; and
(e)one Ayurveda specialist grade doctor each from the specialist grade of the following training centresnominated by the Commissioner of Ayurveda :-
(i)Ayurveda Teaching Hospital Colombo;
(ii)Ayurveda Teaching Hospital Gampaha;
(iii)Bandaranaike Memorial Ayurveda Research Institute.
(2)The Board of Study of Siddha Medicine shall consist of the following persons :-
(a)the Director who shall be an ex - officio member;

(b)two members from the Unit of Siddha Medicine, University of Jaffna established under the Act, electedfrom among the Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors, and Senior Lecturers at the meetingchaired by the Head of the unit;

(c)two members from the Unit of Siddha Medicine, Trincomalee Campus, Eastern University establishedunder the Act, elected from among the Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors, and SeniorLecturers at the meeting chaired by the Head of the unit;
(d)Senior Professor, Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Lecturer from each Department of :-
(i)Noi Naadal Chiktsai;(ii)Virana Chikitsai;(iii)Kuzhanthai Maruthuvam and Mahalir Maruthuram;(iv)Gunapadam;(v)Moola Thatthuvam,
In the Unit of Siddha Medicine, Jaffna and Trincomalee established under the Act, nominated by the Headof the Unit in that order on the recomendation of the relevant Department of Study; and

(3)The Board of study of Unani Medicine shall consist of the following persons :-
(a)the Director who shall be an ex-officio member;

(b)two members from the Branch of Unani Medicine of the Institute of Indigenous Medicine, Colomboestablished under the Act, elected from among the Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors,and Senior Lecturers at the meeting chaired by the Director of the Institute;
(c)a Senior Professor, Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Lecturer from each Department of Study of.

In the Institute of Indigenous Medicine, Colombo established under the Act, nominated by the Director ofthe Institute in that order on the recomendation of the relevant Department of Study; and
(d)One Unani specialist grade doctor each from the specialist grade of the following training centres nomi-nated by the Commissioner of Ayurveda :-
(i)Ayurveda Teaching Hospital Colombo;
(ii)Bandaranaike Memorial Ayurveda Research Institute.
(4)Appointment of members to the Board of Study :-

(a)Nominees of an academic department in a Board of Study shall be selected by the respective Directors,Heads of undergraduate Institutes or Units in consultation with the academic staff members who satisfythe requirements stipulated to be a trainer and forwarded to the Director of the Institute.

(b)Nominees from the training centre of the Ministry of Indigenous Medicine shall be selected from amongspecialist grade doctors who satisfy requirements stipulated to be a trainer, at a meeting chaired by theDirector of the Hospital or Head of the centre. Such names shall be forwarded to the Director of theInstitute by the Commissioner of Ayurveda.

(5)Any Board of Study may, with the concurrence of the Board, co-opt maximum three persons for a period of oneyear for a specified purpose. No person so co-opted shall have the right to stand for election or to vote at any meeting of suchBoard of Study.

(6) (a) Any member of a Board of Study shall, unless he vacates the office earlier, hold the office for a term of three yearsreckoned from the date of this election or appointment and be eligible for re-election or re-appointment :

Provided however, that if any elected or appointed member vacates his office prior to the expiry of his term, hissuccessor shall, unless he vacates his office earlier, hold the office for the unexpired portion of the term of the office of hispredecessor;

Provided further, that each elected or appointed member shall hold the office so long as he retains the status ormembership by virtue of which he was eligible for election appointment as a member of the Board of Study, and shall ceaseto be a member on resignation, retirement or transfer from the hospital, Institute, University or Department of Study.
(b)Any member of a Board of Study may resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to theDirector.

(c)Any elected or appointed member of a Board of Study, who without leave of absence fails attend threeconsecutive meetings of the Board of Study, shall be deemed to have vacated his office as a member of the Board of Studyand the Director shall take such action to appoint a suitable person to fill such vacancy.

(d)In instances where the designated number of members cannot be appointed to a Board of Study or aSpeciality Board due to any valid reason, the Board shall have the power to appont qualified persons to fill such vacanciesin consultation with the relevant Board of Study or the Speciality Board.
(e)The Board shall have the power to dissolve a Board of Study or remove a member of a Board of Study ona vote of censure passed by not less than two - thirds of the total membership of the Board.
(7) (a) Each Board of Study shall have a Chairman who shall be elected by the members of that Board of Study from
among its members.
(b) The terms of the office of the Chairman shall be the term of the office of the Board of Study.
(8) (a) Each Board of Study shall have a Secretary who shall be a member of the Board of Study appointed by the Board
upon the recommendation of the appropriate Board of Study.
(b) The terms of the office of the Secretary shall be the term of the office of the Board of Study.
(9)The quorum of any meeting of any Board of Study constituted under subparagraph (1), (2) and (3) shall be onethird of the membership, excluding the co-opted members, if any.
(10)Each Board of Study shall meet whenever necessary, so however that it meets on not less than ten occasionsin each year.

14. (1) Subject to the provisions of the Act and of any appropriate instrument, each Board of Study shall have controland general direction of instruction, education, research and examinations in respect of the specialities of Ayurveda, Siddhaand Unani systems of Medicine concerned.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the powers conferred upon it by sub-paragraph (1) each Board of Study
shall exercise, perform and discharge the following powers, duties and functions in the specialities of Ayurveda,Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine concerned:-
(a)consider and report on any matter referred to it by the Board.
(b) present recommendations and a report to the Board on all matters connected with the courses of study
traning programmes or programmes and examinations in the relevant speciality;

(c)recommend the appointment of committees, which may include persons other than members of the Boardof Study for the purpose of considering and reporting on any special subject or subjects related to therelevant speciality;
(d) recommend to the Board the requirements for the admission of students to courses of study and examinatios;

(e)draft Regulations relating to courses of study and examinations in the relevant speciality and to submitsuch drafts to the Board;(f)recommend to the Board such persons who are suitable for recognition as trainers and examiners;

(g) recommend to the Board such persons who, having passed the prescribed examinations in the relevant

speciality and having satisfied other prescribed conditions, are eligible for the award of postgraduatedegrees, postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and oher academic distinctions in thatspeciality;
(h) recommend to the Board the mode and conditios of competition for fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions,
bursaries, medals and other prizes;
(i)recommend to the Board, the names of persons suitable for the award of fellowships, scholarships,exhibitions, bursaries medals and other prizes; and
(j)recommend to the Board-

(i)schemes for the reorganization of existing Boards of Study, and the organization of new Boards ofStudy; and(ii)the assignment of specilities of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems of medicine to therespective Boards of Study.
(3) With the approval of the relevant Board of Study, the Board shall establish Speciality Board in respect of
specialities and-
(a)each Speciality Board shall function under the general directions of a relevant Board of Study establishedby the Board in respect of specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani sytems of Medicine;
(b) where a Speciality Board has been extablished in respect of a speciality in which instruction, education,
training and evaluation are carried out under the general direction of a relevant Board of Study, suchSpeciality Board shall consist of ten members as follows:-
(i)the Director;

(ii)six members to be nominated by the relevant Board of Study approved by the Board of whom atleast three members shall be specialist grade doctors from the relevant speciality and shall benominated from among those who are being, or had been employed in any of theundergaduate institutes, Units of Ayurveda, Siddha or Unani sytems of Medicine establishedunder the Act or training centres of the Ministry of Indigenous Medicine;
(iii)three members nominated by the Board from among the specialist grade doctors in the relevantspeciality;

(c)each Speciality Board shall have a Chairman and Secretary who shall be elected by the members of theSpeciality Board from among its members and the tenure of the office shall be the tenure of the SpecialityBoard;
(d) quorum of any meeting of a Speciality Board shall be one third of the total membership excluding the co-
opted members, if any;
(e)tenure of the office of a Specility Board shall expire on the date of expiry of the tenure of the office of theBoard of Study;
(f)each Speciality Board shall hold a minimum of six meetings each year;
(g) each Speciality Board may recommend co-opting of specialists for a specific purpose and for a specified
period and no person so co-opted shall have the right to stand for election or vote at any meeing of theSpeciality Board;
(h) in instances, where a member of a Speciality Board who is not a member of a relevant Board of Study

concerned is assigned to present matters pertaining to the Speciality Board at a meeing of the relevantBoard of Study such nominee shall be deemed to have been duly co-opted for that specitic presenationand on completion of such presentation he ceases to be a co-opted member;
(i)the Board shall have the power to dissolve a Speciality Board or remove a member of a Speciality Boardon a vote of censure passed by not less than two thirds of the total membership of the Board.

(4)Subject to the provisions of the Act, Ordinance or any appropriate instrument and the general directions andcontrol of the Board of Study each Speciality Board shall perform and discharge the following functions:-
(a)submit recommendations and a report to the relevant Board of Study on all matters concerned with coursesof study,training programmes, curricula and examinations related to the speciality;
(b) recommend the appointment of sub-committees, when relevant, which may include persons other than
members of the Speciality Board for the purpose of considering and reporting on a special subject to thespeciality, if any;
(c)recommend to the Board of Study the requirements for admission of trainees to courses of study, trainingprogrammes and examinations;
(d) submit to the Board of Study draft regulations relating to courses of study and examinations;
(e)recommend to the Board of Study such persons who are suitable for recognition as trainers and examinersin conformity with the general rules and regulations governing such fuctions; and
(f)shall report on mattes being referred to the Speciality Board by the Board of Study concerned or the Board.
15.The financial year of the Institute shall be the same as the financial year of the Government.
16. (1) The institute shall have a fund to be called the Postgradute Institute of Indigenous Medicine Fund (hereinafter
referred to as the "Fund"), into which shall be paid-
(a)fees to be paid to the Institute in accordance with the provisions of ay appropriate instrument;
(b) income from endowments;
(c)moneys provided by the Parliament and disbursed by the Commission as grants in aid of the Institute;
(d) all other moneys belonging to the Institute from whatever source derved.
(2) A summary of all sums of money paid to the Fund within the course of a particular month, classified under the
appropriate heads of revenue, shall before the end of the next ensuing month be submitted by the Director tothe Commission for its information.
17.It shall be the duty of the Director-
(a)to keep the accounts of the Insitute in such form and manner as may be prescribed by Ordinance;
(b) to receive all moneys paid into the Fund and to credit such moneys to the proper heads of accounts;
(c)to make all authorized payments;
(d) to prepare for the Board such triennil estimates as are required by the Commission and the annual financial
appropriations for the ensuing year:

Provided however, that income derived from grants made for specific purposes or from endowments for specific objects,shall be separately accounted for in the accounts of the Institute, and that no payment shall be made from such income forthe general purposes of the Institute or for any purpose or object other than for which such grants or endowments wererespectively made.

18. (1)The Institute shall prepare an annual statement of accounts, and statistics relating to its activities in suchform and manner and containing such particulars as the Commission may from time to time specify.
(2)The books of accounts of the Institute shall be in the office of the Institute.

19. Such provisions of Part XIII of the Act as are relevant to the auditing of the accounts of a higher educationalinstitution shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to and in relation to the auditing of the accounts of the Institute.

20. (1)The staff of the Institute shall consist of such officers and other employees as it may with the concurrenceof the University and the approval of the Commission deem necessary for the efficient exercise, discharge and performanceof the powers, duties and functions of the Institute.

(2)The staff of the Institute shall be provided on release by the University from among its own staff or beappointed by the Commission or the University, as the case may be. The provisions of part X of the Actshall, mutatis mutandis, apply to and in relation to appointment to the staff of the Institute.

(3)Where the services of an officer or other employee of the University have been provided to the Istitute ona full-time basis, the Institute shall pay him the salary and the allowances of his substantive post in theUniversity. In any other case, the Institute may pay the officer or other employee concerned, suchallowance as it may determine in consultation with the University and with the approval of theCommission.
(4)The staff of the Institute shall be subject to the direction and the disciplinary control of the Director.

21. If any question arises as to whether any person has been duly elected, appoined, nominated or co-opted or asto whether any person is entitled to be, a member of any Authority or other body of the Intitute, such question shall bereferred to the Commission in the event the Board is unable to resolve the question raised whose decision thereof shall befinal.

22. No act, resolution or proceeding of any Authority or other body of the Institute, shall be invalidated merely byreason of the existence of a vacancy or of vacancies among its members or of any defects in the appoitment of such member.

23. Upon the coming into operation of this Ordinance, the power to grant and to confer postgraduate degrees,postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions in the specialities of Ayurveda Siddha andUnani systems of Medicine shall be vested solely in the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Provided however,-
(1) that the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka, shall grant and confer such postgraduate degrees, postghraduate
diplomas, pstgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions only upon the recommendation of theInstitute.
(2) that any University established or deemed to be established under the Act, may grant and confer such

postgraduate degrees, postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and other academic distinctions inany specialities, of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine in respect of which no Board of Studyhas been established by the Institute under the provisions of paragraph 13.
(3) that any University established or deemed to be established under the Act, may grant and confer postgraduate

degrees based wholly or partly upon research in any speciality of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems ofMedicine, whether or not a Board of Study in respect of such speciality has been established by the Instituteunder the provisions of paragraph 13; and
(4) that academic distinctions in the specialities of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems of Medicine my be
granted by professional bodies by arrangment with the Institute and the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka, andwith the concurrence of the Commission.
24. In this Ordinance-
" Act" means the Universities Act, No. 16 of 1978;
" appropriate instrument" means any Order, Ordinance, Statute, By-law, Regulation or Rule made in accordance withthe provisons of the Act;
"Commssion" means the University Grants Commision established under the Universities Act;

" Examiner" mean a person having five years experience after Board Cerfification or equivalent qualifications oreligible for privileges of Board Certification and who shall be in active service in any University or in the Ministry ofIndigenous Medicine;
